title: Survey highlights AI's potential to advance accessibility in work and learning
excerpt: As artificial intelligence becomes part of how people work, learn and solve problems, a new University of Phoenix survey conducted by The Harris Poll finds that recent working learners see meaningful opportunities for AI to support accessibility.
content_html:
As artificial intelligence becomes part of how people work, learn and solve problems, a new University of Phoenix survey conducted by The Harris Poll finds that recent working learners see meaningful opportunities for AI to support accessibility.

The survey was designed to understand the impact of AI in the workplace and learning environments on accessibility, defined as ensuring digital content, tools and resources, including AI tools and outputs, are usable by people with different abilities through inclusive design, use of assistive technology or conformance with accessibility standards, such as the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG).

The findings were released ahead of the 36th anniversary of the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) on July 26.

The survey was conducted among 1,019 U.S. employed adults who completed a professionally presented training or school course in the past 12 months ("recent working learners").

While the findings point to optimism about AI's accessibility potential, they also reveal an opportunity for clearer organizational guidance: 45% of respondents say accessibility is absent from, unclear in or they are uncertain whether it is covered by their workplace AI policies.

"The reality is that accessibility benefits everyone," said Kelly Hermann, vice president of accessibility and student affairs at University of Phoenix.

"If accessibility is built in from the beginning, organizations are more likely to create AI-enabled environments that are universally usable. Clearer content, better summaries, accurate captions, and multiple formats can help workers and learners with disabilities, but they also help busy adults, multilingual learners, mobile users, and anyone trying to absorb information quickly."

Key findings from the survey include:

  • Workers see AI's accessibility potential: 89% of recent working learners identify workflows that could benefit from AI and accessibility tools, especially creating accessible documents, presentations, websites or learning materials (38%), presenting information in different formats such as plain language, audio, summaries or translations (33%), and training employees or learners on accessibility practices (30%).
  • AI may help build accessibility awareness: Among those already using AI in the workplace, 60% say AI has improved their knowledge of and ability to use accessibility standards and guidelines.
  • Accessibility is not always clear in workplace AI policies: 45% of recent working learners say accessibility is absent from, unclear in or they are uncertain whether it is covered by their workplace AI policies.
  • AI tools may not yet fully support different access needs: Among those who use workplace AI tools, only about a quarter of survey respondents (27%) say AI tools available through their workplace or professional learning environment support people with disabilities very well.
  • Human oversight remains important: 36% of recent working learners say human review for important decisions or high-impact work should be part of responsible AI use at work or school.
  • Workers also recognize how AI and accessibility can have an impact on their own career journey: 90% of recent working learners identify AI and accessibility skills that would be valuable in their current or desired career field, including 45% who see value in understanding when AI-generated content needs human review.

Why accessibility is essential to responsible AI adoption

As AI tools are used to draft documents, summarize information, generate captions and transcripts, create image descriptions, support learning and assist with workplace tasks, accessibility becomes central to responsible use. Poorly implemented AI can also create or amplify barriers, including inaccessible content, inaccurate summaries, biased outputs and tools that do not work effectively with assistive technologies.

"Responsible AI is not only about productivity," Hermann said. "It is about whether the technology works for the people who need to use it. AI can help create more accessible materials and more flexible ways to engage with information, but it still requires clear policies, practical training and human judgment to make sure the outputs are accurate, applicable and usable."

What the findings mean for employers and educators

The survey suggests that organizations have an opportunity to align AI adoption with supportive design, accessibility practices and workforce training. Employers and educators can take immediate steps by:

  • Naming accessibility directly in AI policies and guidance.
  • Choosing AI tools with accessibility and assistive technology compatibility in mind.
  • Training workers and learners to create, check and improve accessible AI-generated content.
  • Making support pathways clear for people who experience barriers using AI tools.
  • Keeping human review in place for important decisions, high-impact work and accessibility-sensitive outputs.

The survey also found workers want practical AI training. The most helpful resources identified by recent working learners include real-world examples from their field or industry (36%), hands-on practice using realistic workplace scenarios (34%) and step-by-step demonstrations of common tasks (33%).

content_html_zh:
随着人工智能成为人们工作、学习和解决问题方式的一部分，凤凰城大学哈里斯民意调查进行的一项新调查发现，最近的工作学习者看到了人工智能支持无障碍的有意义的机会。

该调查旨在了解人工智能在工作场所和学习环境中对无障碍的影响，无障碍的定义是通过包容性设计、使用辅助技术或遵守无障碍标准（例如《网络内容无障碍指南》（WCAG）），确保数字内容、工具和资源（包括人工智能工具和输出）可供不同能力的人使用。

该调查结果于 7 月 26 日《美国残疾人法案》(ADA) 36 周年纪念日之前发布。

该调查针对 1,019 名在过去 12 个月内完成专业培训或学校课程的美国就业成年人（“近期工作学习者”）进行。

虽然调查结果表明人们对人工智能的可访问性潜力持乐观态度，但它们也揭示了获得更清晰的组织指导的机会：45％的受访者表示，可访问性不存在、不清楚或不确定其工作场所人工智能政策是否涵盖可访问性。

菲尼克斯大学负责无障碍和学生事务的副校长凯利·赫尔曼 (Kelly Hermann) 表示：“现实情况是，无障碍对每个人都有好处。”

“如果从一开始就内置可访问性，组织就更有可能创建普遍可用的人工智能环境。 更清晰的内容、更好的摘要、准确的标题和多种格式可以帮助残疾工人和学习者，但它们也可以帮助忙碌的成年人、多语言学习者、移动用户以及任何试图快速吸收信息的人。”

调查的主要结果包括：

  • 员工看到了人工智能的无障碍潜力：89% 的近期工作学习者认为可以从人工智能和无障碍工具中受益的工作流程，特别是创建无障碍文档、演示文稿、网站或学习材料 (38%)，以不同格式呈现信息，如简单语言、音频、摘要或翻译 (33%)，以及对员工或学习者进行无障碍实践培训 (30%)。
  • 人工智能可能有助于建立无障碍意识：在已经在工作场所使用人工智能的人中，60% 的人表示人工智能提高了他们对无障碍标准和指南的了解和使用能力。
  • 工作场所人工智能政策中的可访问性并不总是明确的：45% 的最近在职学习者表示，可访问性不存在、不清楚或不确定是否包含在工作场所人工智能政策中。
  • 人工智能工具可能尚未完全支持不同的访问需求：在使用工作场所人工智能工具的人中，只有约四分之一的受访者 (27%) 表示，通过其工作场所或专业学习环境提供的人工智能工具可以很好地支持残疾人。
  • 人类监督仍然很重要：36% 的近期工作学习者表示，对重要决策或高影响力工作的人工审查应该成为工作或学校负责任地使用人工智能的一部分。
  • 员工还认识到人工智能和可访问性如何对他们自己的职业生涯产生影响：90% 的近期在职学习者认为人工智能和可访问性技能对他们当前或想要的职业领域很有价值，其中 45% 的人认为理解人工智能生成的内容何时需要人工审核是有价值的。

为什么可访问性对于负责任的人工智能采用至关重要

由于人工智能工具用于起草文档、总结信息、生成标题和文字记录、创建图像描述、支持学习和协助完成工作场所任务，因此可访问性成为负责任使用的核心。 人工智能实施不当还会造成或扩大障碍，包括无法访问的内容、不准确的摘要、有偏见的输出以及无法与辅助技术有效配合的工具。

“负责任的人工智能不仅仅关乎生产力，”赫尔曼说。 “问题在于该技术是否适合需要使用它的人。 人工智能可以帮助创建更容易获取的材料和更灵活的信息交互方式，但它仍然需要明确的政策、实际培训和人类判断，以确保输出准确、适用和可用。”

研究结果对雇主和教育工作者意味着什么

该调查表明，组织有机会将人工智能的采用与支持性设计、可访问性实践和劳动力培训结合起来。 雇主和教育工作者可以通过以下方式立即采取措施：

  • 直接在人工智能政策和指南中命名可访问性。
  • 选择人工智能工具时要考虑到可访问性和辅助技术兼容性。
  • 培训工作人员和学习者创建、检查和改进可访问的人工智能生成的内容。
  • 为在使用人工智能工具时遇到障碍的人们提供清晰的支持途径。
  • 对重要决策、高影响力工作和可访问性敏感的输出进行人工审查。

调查还发现，员工希望接受实用的人工智能培训。 最近在职学习者发现的最有用的资源包括来自其领域或行业的真实示例（36%）、使用现实工作场所场景的实践练习（34%）以及常见任务的分步演示（33%）。
